> Case study · OSINT · Field infiltration + attribution · Anonymized
⚠️ All names, surnames, countries, cities, and any identifying details of individuals mentioned in this article have been altered or are entirely fictional for anonymization purposes. Any resemblance to real persons is purely coincidental. The geographic scope of the cases, the investigative context, and the events described are based on real operations. All tools, methodologies, and operational logic presented in this article are real and were used as part of the investigation.
## Prologue. Where This Knowledge Comes From Before getting to the investigation itself — context matters. This is not theory. This is not something learned from reports or textbooks. This is experience built from inside real operations. I started my career in law enforcement at the ground level — first in juvenile prevention, then as a community police officer. It was honest work. Necessary work. Over time, I realised I wanted to go deeper into complex investigations and analytical work. Passing the selection into the Strategic Investigations Department changed everything. That was the point where my path toward OSINT truly began. Our unit focused on transnational and ethnic organised crime groups. The work was operational, not theoretical: surveillance, wiretaps, physical infiltration, vehicle tracking, installation of monitoring equipment, deployment of spyware. It wasn't easy work. But it was real. One case, in particular, defined that period of my career. We spent nearly two years dismantling a large-scale fraudulent call centre whose operators impersonated law enforcement officers and targeted victims across multiple European and post-Soviet countries. Two years of surveillance. Two years of evidence building. Two years of systematic work — until the structure collapsed. And when it did — every individual involved was identified, detained, and brought to justice. For those interested in the public side of that operation, several media reports covered the takedown and the arrests: - [nashreporter.com — fraudulent call centres in Kamianske](https://nashreporter.com/kryminal/u-kamyanskomu-shahrajski-kol-czentry-vyduryuvaly-groshi-v-inozemcziv-video-67250) - [com1.org.ua — call centre in Kamianske defrauded Latvians](https://com1.org.ua/moshennycheskyj-koll-tsentr-v-kamenskom-obmanyval-latyshej/) - [detective-info.com.ua — Dnipro region call centre linked to Lasha Svan](https://detective-info.com.ua/na-dnipropetrovshhini-vikrili-call-czentr-providnikom-yakogo-vvazhayut-dovirenu-osobu-zlodiya-v-zakoni-lashi-svana.html) - [ukrinform.ua — Lithuanians defrauded of 11 million UAH](https://www.ukrinform.ua/rubric-society/3970096-osukali-gromadan-litvi-na-11-miljoniv-policia-zatrimala-pracivnikiv-sahrajskogo-sallcentru.html) These reports reflect only the surface. The operational work behind them took nearly two years. After leaving law enforcement, I transitioned into OSINT and SOCMINT as a freelancer and later worked with a private detective agency. That experience — both inside official investigations and outside of them — is what led directly to the case you are about to read. --- ## Part I. Inside the Operation ### How a Crypto Scam Call Centre Works At that time, some people within my extended circle were involved in operations like this. I made a decision to go inside — not as a law enforcement officer, and not with a badge, but as someone willing to understand how the system works from within. It was a civilian-level infiltration. And it worked. There was no suspicion, no resistance. On the contrary, I was perceived as a potential recruit — someone who could grow within the structure. That gave me a very limited window: **two days to observe, understand, and retain everything** before stepping away without raising questions. What I saw during that time was not chaos, not improvisation, and not random activity. It was a system — structured, disciplined, and scalable, designed to extract money from people with precision. ### The Three-Tier Structure The operation is built as a structured, role-based system with a clear hierarchy and distribution of responsibilities. Each role has a defined function, specific limits of authority, and a measurable outcome. At its core, the system consists of three levels. **Cold Caller ("Kholodka")** — entry-level operator responsible for initial contact. Their role is to identify potential targets, initiate communication, and build trust over time. This is not a one-time interaction but a long-term process that can last weeks or even months. The objective is to prepare the victim psychologically and transfer them to the next stage. Typically, one Closer is supported by two to five Cold Callers. **Closer ("Klouzer")** — mid-level operator who presents themselves as a "crypto expert." This role carries authority. The Closer builds on the trust established by the Cold Caller and moves the victim toward a financial decision. Their primary objective is conversion — turning trust into money. **Control ("Pult")** — senior-level operator. Usually someone who has progressed through all previous roles. This position oversees the entire operation: monitoring conversations, coordinating team activity in real time, and managing financial flows. Control ensures discipline, consistency, and performance across the system. This structure is not accidental. It is designed for efficiency, scalability, and sustained psychological pressure on the target. Each role isolates responsibility: Cold Callers build emotional connection, Closers convert that trust into financial action, and Control maintains oversight and operational control. The separation also reduces risk. No single operator has full visibility of the entire scheme, while Control retains centralized awareness. From an operational perspective, this model closely resembles legitimate sales organisations — with lead generation, relationship building, and conversion — but applied to systematic fraud. ### How It Works: Step by Step What follows is not a simplified explanation. It is a reconstruction of the operational workflow as it is actually executed inside a crypto scam call centre. The process is structured, repeatable, and refined through constant practice. **Step 1. Building the Alter-Ego.** Every operation begins with identity construction. A Cold Caller does not simply create a fake name — they build a complete, internally consistent persona: country and city of origin, family background, education and career path, personal struggles and turning points. Special attention is given to realism. Operators study the chosen location in detail: landmarks, lifestyle, cultural references, even local slang. The target country is assigned by a senior operator. The most important part of the legend is the transition story — how the persona "discovered" cryptocurrency through a trusted contact (the Closer) and achieved financial success. This narrative will later be reused as a persuasion tool. **Step 2. Identity Infrastructure and Face Preparation.** The operation relies on scale. Each Cold Caller maintains between 10 and 100+ accounts across platforms, with Telegram as the primary channel. To support credibility, operators use face-generation and face-mapping technologies. A "donor" is selected — a real person found via social media whose appearance closely matches the operator. This allows two things: use of modified static images that avoid direct reverse search detection, and preparation for live video calls using face overlay technologies. The objective is simple: remove doubt at any stage of interaction. **Step 3. Target Environment Selection.** Cold Callers identify environments where real people communicate organically. Typically, this involves joining dozens of Telegram groups, channels, and chats — often 50 or more. Topics are selected based on the operator's ability to engage: psychology, finance, travel, law, IT. Accounts are "warmed up" for several days before active engagement begins. Without this, Telegram's internal systems may flag or restrict activity. **Step 4. Initial Contact and Social Positioning.** The operator does not approach victims directly with an offer. Instead, they integrate into the community: commenting on discussions, providing advice, asking questions, sharing opinions. This creates visibility and perceived authenticity. From there, conversations gradually move into private messages. The initial phase can last weeks or months. In high-value cases, even longer. At this stage, there is no mention of money. The objective is positioning — becoming a familiar and trusted presence. **Step 5. Psychological Conditioning.** Once trust is established, the operation enters its most critical phase. This is the point where the interaction shifts from communication to influence. The victim begins to open up. They share personal details: stress at work, financial instability, dissatisfaction with life, relationship problems, the desire to "make a difference". For the operator, this is not conversation — this is **data collection**. Every detail becomes a lever. The Cold Caller applies one of the core techniques: **mirroring**. "I went through the same situation" — "I know exactly how that feels" — "I was stuck like that for years". This is not mere empathy. It is structured. The operator does not just agree — they reconstruct the victim's emotional state and reflect it back in a controlled form. The goal is simple: create the illusion of deep understanding. Once a person feels understood, they lower their defenses. The operator gradually aligns their emotional tone with the victim: if the victim is frustrated → they validate frustration; if the victim is hopeful → they amplify hope; if the victim is insecure → they provide reassurance. This creates emotional dependency. The victim begins to see the operator not as a stranger, but as someone who is "on the same wavelength". Only after this connection is established, the operator introduces the key element — their personal "success story". But it is not presented as a pitch. It is presented as a natural continuation of the conversation: "At some point, I realised I had to change something" — "That's when I met someone who introduced me to crypto" — "I didn't believe it at first either". The victim recognises themselves in this story. This is intentional. The story is designed as a psychological mirror. Over time, the operator begins to reshape the victim's perception of reality. Not through pressure — through repetition and framing. Crypto is no longer presented as risk. It is presented as opportunity, solution, way out. At the same time, the victim's current life is subtly reframed as stagnant, limiting, "wasting potential". This creates an internal contrast: current life vs possible future. And the operator positions themselves as the bridge between the two. One of the most important principles: **at this stage, no one is asking for money**. And that is exactly why it works. The victim does not feel targeted. They feel understood, supported, connected. By the time money is even mentioned, the decision is already emotionally prepared. This level of interaction is not improvisation. Operators are trained. Inside these call centres they study basic behavioural psychology, practice dialogue scenarios, rehearse objections, train storytelling. In many cases, they are given "homework": write and refine their legend, practice emotional responses, simulate conversations with colleagues. What looks like a natural conversation is, in reality, a rehearsed process. By the end of this stage, the victim does not feel manipulated. They feel lucky. They believe they met the right person at the right time who understands them and wants to help. And that belief is what makes everything that follows possible. **Step 6. Transfer to the Closer.** Once the victim shows genuine interest, a critical transition takes place. The Cold Caller carefully positions themselves as someone who is "not an expert," but who knows a trusted person with real experience in crypto. This is framed as concern, not escalation: "I don't want you to make a mistake" — "You should speak to someone who actually understands the market". The victim is then given the Closer's Telegram contact. From this moment, the dynamic of the interaction changes completely. If the Cold Caller represents emotional connection, the Closer represents **authority**. Calm, confident, and controlled — the Closer presents themselves as a professional investor. They do not apply pressure immediately. Instead, they begin with structured questions: prior investment experience, income level, financial goals. This creates the illusion of a legitimate advisory process. The victim is then guided to register on a crypto platform and make an initial deposit, typically between $100 and $1,000. This is where the operation becomes highly sophisticated. Unlike basic scams, the first results are real: the balance appears to grow, "investments" show profit, the victim is allowed to withdraw funds. In some cases, the Closer even encourages a withdrawal: "Try taking some profit to see how it works". This is intentional. The victim receives tangible proof — money arrives, can be spent, transferred, touched. At this exact moment, the primary barrier collapses: distrust. Psychologically, the victim no longer perceives risk. They perceive a **verified opportunity**. **Step 7. Coordinated Pressure.** Once trust is established, the operation shifts into escalation. The Cold Caller and Closer begin working as a coordinated unit. Importantly, they are not independent actors — they are in the same office, often communicating in real time. The victim is now influenced from two directions simultaneously. From the Cold Caller: emotional support, empathy, personal connection. From the Closer: authority, confidence, financial guidance. This dual-layer influence significantly increases compliance. The victim does not feel pressured — they feel guided. At this stage, the financial expectations begin to grow. If the victim has available funds, they are gradually encouraged to increase investment amounts. If funds are limited, additional mechanisms are introduced: suggestions to take loans, framing the opportunity as "once in a lifetime", encouragement to liquidate assets (vehicles, valuables, savings). Special attention is given to emotional triggers: fear of missing out, desire for financial breakthrough, trust in people who have already "proven" results. Over time, the victim reaches a point where they are willing to commit significantly more than they originally intended. **Step 8. The Final Investment Trap.** Once the victim is fully conditioned, the final stage is introduced. They are presented with an "exclusive opportunity" — often framed as time-sensitive and limited. This is usually accompanied by an email with a formal-looking offer, structured explanations, justification for why this opportunity is available specifically to them. Promised returns are typically in the range of +30% to +40% or higher. From a rational standpoint, this is unrealistic. But at this stage, rational thinking no longer drives decision-making. The victim has already seen profits, has successfully withdrawn funds, trusts the Closer, is emotionally invested. In their perception, this is not a risk. It is the next logical step. The transfer process is fully controlled. The Closer guides the victim step by step: where to click, which wallet to use, how much to transfer. Funds are sent directly to wallets controlled by the scammers. After that: funds are held temporarily, cycled through multiple transactions, gradually withdrawn in portions. This reduces the risk of detection, avoids platform restrictions, and distributes funds across the operation. **Step 9. Extraction Phase.** Even after a significant transfer, the process does not stop. In fact, this is where the final extraction begins. The operators understand they have a limited window before the victim realises what has happened. During this period, they maintain active communication: promising imminent profits, reinforcing belief in the process, creating a sense that success is "just around the corner". The victim is pushed further: to take additional loans, to borrow from friends and family, to bring in new participants. A common tactic: "If you increase your position now, you can recover everything faster". The narrative remains consistent: the Closer is "investing alongside" the victim, their interests are "aligned", they are "working together" toward profit. This sustains trust until the very end. The objective is simple: extract maximum value before the illusion collapses. After that, communication either fades or transitions into a secondary scam phase — such as fabricated "withdrawal issues" designed to extract even more money. ### What This Really Is When you look at all nine steps together, one thing becomes clear: this is not a "scam" in the simple sense. It is a **structured system of psychological manipulation** designed to move a person from first contact to full financial compliance. There is no randomness, no improvisation, no luck. Every stage has a purpose, every message has intent, every pause and response is part of a controlled sequence. The victim is not convinced in a single moment — they are gradually moved into a different perception of reality. By the time money is transferred, the decision has already been made. Not logically, but emotionally. From the outside, it looks simple: "just don't send the money". From the inside, it feels completely different: "I trust this person, I've seen it work, I understand what I'm doing". That gap between perception and reality is exactly where this system operates — and that is why it works, regardless of country, background, or level of education. --- ## Part II. My Friend Was Next Some time later, this stopped being just analysis. It became personal. During a regular family video call, a close friend of mine — an economist living abroad — casually mentioned that "things were about to change" for him. The way he said it was familiar. Too familiar. I had heard that tone before — confidence mixed with excitement, but built on something artificial. I asked a few questions. The answers were enough. He told me about a person he had met on Telegram. They had been talking for weeks. Conversations felt natural, supportive. At some point, the topic shifted to crypto. Slowly. Without pressure. Exactly as I had seen it done before. I tried to stop it immediately. Explained the scheme. Broke it down step by step. Showed where it leads. **It didn't work.** The psychological conditioning had already done its job. He trusted that "Telegram contact" more than he trusted me. This is the moment most people don't understand. Intelligence does not protect you here. Education does not protect you. Experience does not protect you. If the process is executed correctly, **anyone** can be pulled into it. The situation escalated when he mentioned the amount he was planning to invest: **$30,000**. At that point, this was no longer a conversation. It was a race against time. The only reason the situation didn't end there was his wife. She listened. She questioned. She saw the inconsistency. And eventually, she convinced him to let me take a closer look. He agreed, but without full belief. Not because he trusted me — but because he wanted confirmation that everything was legitimate. That was enough. At that moment, I knew one thing: this was no longer theory. This was an active operation, with a real victim, real money, and a very short window before the final step. And that meant only one option — move fast. --- ## Part III. The Investigation ### Stage 1 — Username to Phone Number Starting point: Telegram username. Reverse lookup → linked phone number extracted. Immediate inconsistency: numbering origin does not match declared geography. Different region, different telecom pattern — legend integrity already compromised. ![Telegram reverse lookup — the phone number origin does not match the declared country](/img/uploads/cases/crypto-scam-01-telegram-phone.png) Next — account behaviour. Group memberships and subscriptions show a controlled distribution: crypto, banking, IT-related channels. No deviation, no personal interests, no noise. ![Group memberships — narrowly clustered around crypto, banking, and IT channels. No personal noise](/img/uploads/cases/crypto-scam-02-telegram-groups.png) That matters. Real users are inconsistent — mixed interests, inactive periods, fragmented behaviour. Here — only functional clustering around scam-relevant domains. **The account is not empty. It is curated.** No personal history, no created groups, no identity continuity. Everything points to an account built for operation, not for presence. Check against Telegram breach datasets → no hits. Likely a fresh number or not yet exposed in indexed leaks. At this stage: no attribution, but the pattern is already clear — broken legend + controlled behavioural footprint, consistent with organised scam infrastructure. ### Stage 2 — Reverse Image Search Next vector — profile image. Reverse face search returned a match, but the identified person was located in a completely different country than the one claimed. No overlap, no logical connection. At this point, the task was not attribution, but integrity check. Direct comparison showed something more interesting: the face was similar, but not identical. Structure matched, details didn't. That rules out a simple stolen photo. ![Face similarity test — 33% match. The photo is a modified version of a real person's image, not a direct steal](/img/uploads/cases/crypto-scam-03-face-similarity.png) This is a known pattern — **modified source image**. A real person is used as a base, but the image is slightly altered to reduce reverse-search accuracy. Enough to pass as real, but not enough to be traced directly. That also aligns with operational behaviour: static images are "softened" versions, while the real face (or deepfake layer) is reserved for live interaction. Important decision here — no confrontation. Breaking the interaction at this stage would kill access. The subject still believed the identity held, and that assumption needed to stay intact. At this point, the conclusion was clear: the identity was not stolen, but engineered. ### Transition — From Indicators to Proof At this point, the indicators were clear, but insufficient. The legend was inconsistent, the identity layer was engineered, the behavioural profile matched an operational account — but none of this was enough to break the psychological hold. My friend was still not convinced. And that is a critical factor. In cases like this, technical indicators mean nothing if the victim does not accept them. Pushing further with the same approach would only strengthen resistance. **Decision: change the vector.** The objective shifted from analysis to proof. Not theoretical, not analytical — direct, visual, undeniable. Something that bypasses argument entirely. At this stage, the question was no longer "who is this," but "how to force an exposure without alerting the subject." That required using **behaviour**, not data. ### Stage 3. Forcing Exposure At this point, the objective was clear: force identity exposure without triggering defensive behaviour. Direct confrontation was not an option. Any pressure would result in immediate disengagement. The subject still believed the legend was intact — that assumption had to be preserved. The solution came from understanding the environment. Based on direct observation of how these call centres operate, one pattern stands out: **strict discipline**. Fixed schedules, controlled shifts, penalties for delays. Operators function under time pressure. That creates a vulnerability. **Decision: exploit timing.** I instructed my friend to maintain normal communication for several days — no behavioural changes, no escalation. Then identify the exact time window when the subject typically initiated contact. The action itself was simple: initiate a video call approximately **ten minutes before that time** and start screen recording immediately. The logic was straightforward. An operator preparing to initiate contact is focused on outgoing communication, not incoming verification. Add time pressure, and attention drops. Under those conditions, acceptance decisions become automatic. That is where mistakes happen. The result confirmed the assumption. The call was accepted without verification. For a brief moment, the subject appeared on camera before reacting. The response was immediate — verbal reaction, disconnection — but the exposure had already occurred. **One frame was enough.** At that point, the identity layer was no longer under his control. ### Stage 4. OSINT Acceleration Once the real face was captured, the investigation moved from indicators to attribution. Speed increased, but so did precision requirements — mistakes at this stage scale quickly. First step — reverse face search via a Telegram-based OSINT bot. Result: ~78% match, leading to a social media profile and a linked phone number. This was the first pivot from anonymous presence to a real-world identity layer. ![Screen recording of the video call — the captured frame that made attribution possible](/img/uploads/cases/crypto-scam-04-face-frame.png) Next — phone number enrichment using **Manuel Travezaño's Telegram bot** (breach-focused intelligence). The output provided multiple data points: full name, additional phone numbers, and cross-linked services. This confirmed that the number was not isolated, but part of a wider digital footprint. ![Manuel Travezaño's bot output — full name, additional phone numbers, cross-linked services](/img/uploads/cases/crypto-scam-05-manuel-bot.png) Parallel check — Telegram leak bots. The number was cross-referenced against available breach datasets. Partial overlap confirmed presence in leak surfaces, strengthening attribution confidence. Then — email pivot. One of the datasets returned an email address associated with the subject. That email was processed through **OSINT Industries**. Result: expanded profile — linked accounts, behavioural signals, and indirect geolocation indicators through activity patterns. Repeated location references, check-ins, and content interaction pointed consistently to one country and city, contradicting the original legend entirely. ![OSINT Industries — geolocation indicators concentrated on one specific country and city](/img/uploads/cases/crypto-scam-06-osint-industries-map.png) ![OSINT Industries — Google Maps reviews tied to specific establishments in the real country of residence](/img/uploads/cases/crypto-scam-07-google-maps.png) At this stage, fragmentation disappeared. Independent data points began to converge: face → social profile, phone → breach data, email → activity & geolocation. This is the critical moment in any OSINT investigation — when separate weak signals form a coherent identity. Important observation: the subject demonstrated **poor digital hygiene**. Reused identifiers across platforms, presence in multiple leaks, no compartmentalisation. This is typical for low-to-mid level operators in fraud structures — operational discipline exists inside the system, but not outside of it. Final output at this stage: real identity (name), primary and secondary phone numbers, linked email, social media presence, probable real location (country + city). Attribution threshold: sufficient for escalation and evidentiary packaging. --- ## Investigation Summary At this stage, the objective was no longer identification — it was consolidation. All collected data points were structured into a single evidentiary package suitable for handover. The dataset included: - Full communication history with the subject (screenshots + screen recordings), including behavioural patterns and escalation points - Video capture of the subject's real face obtained through controlled exposure - Attributed identity (full name), with supporting links across phone number, social media, and email - Enriched profile including additional phone numbers, linked accounts, and activity indicators - Transaction context — all financial interactions initiated prior to intervention All elements were cross-referenced. No single data point was used in isolation — only converging signals were included in the final package. This reduces false attribution risk and increases evidentiary value. Important detail: the subject identified at this stage represents a **low-level operator** (Cold Caller). However, in structured fraud environments, this is not a limitation — it is an entry point. From an investigative perspective, one confirmed identity is enough to initiate expansion: operator → supervisor (Closer) → control layer → organisers. **The chain always builds forward.** The complete package was transferred to the victim, who proceeded with an official report to law enforcement, including all supporting materials and financial records. At this point, the role of OSINT in this case was complete: identification, validation, and preparation for escalation. --- ## Conclusions for OSINT Professionals **1. Attribution often starts with a trigger event.** In controlled environments — purchased accounts, VPN usage, compartmentalised identities — initial attribution can be extremely limited. In this case, the investigation shifted only after a trigger event: real face exposure during a video call. From that point, OSINT did what it does best — linking, validating, and expanding. The takeaway is not limitation, but sequence: **exposure → pivot → attribution**. **2. Behaviour is a critical entry point.** Technical data alone rarely creates the breakthrough. Behaviour does. Understanding timing, routine, and operational pressure made it possible to create the conditions for that trigger event. This is where OSINT moves beyond tools — into operational thinking. **3. Speed of pivoting defines outcome.** Once the identity layer was exposed, rapid correlation became critical: face → social profile → phone number → breach data → email → activity. Each step reinforced the previous one, turning a single data point into a structured identity. In time-sensitive scenarios, the ability to move quickly between pivots is often the difference between signal and loss. **4. Layered identities require layered validation.** The subject did not rely on a single fake element. The identity was constructed — modified imagery, controlled narrative, selective exposure. This requires parallel validation across multiple vectors, not reliance on a single match or tool. **5. Access enables control.** Maintaining communication with the subject allowed the investigation to develop naturally and reach a controlled exposure point. Breaking contact too early would have removed that opportunity entirely. In practice, access is not just a channel — it is **leverage**. --- ## Conclusions for Everyone Else You do not need to understand OSINT to protect yourself. But you do need to understand how these situations actually work. **1. If you think "this won't happen to me" — you are the target.** These operations are not random. They are structured, trained, and patient. You are not dealing with a "scammer" — you are dealing with a system designed to gain your trust over time. The longer you communicate, the stronger the psychological grip becomes. **2. Trust built online is a construct, not proof.** Weeks or months of conversation, shared interests, emotional support — none of this confirms identity. It confirms one thing only: someone is investing time in you. And in these cases, time is part of the strategy. **3. Nobody can predict crypto profits — nobody.** Any person who tells you "this will grow," "this is guaranteed," or "I will help you earn" is not giving you an opportunity — they are building a scenario. There is no legitimate version of "guaranteed profit" in crypto. **4. Early profit is not success — it is conditioning.** If you invest a small amount and see it grow — even if you withdraw money — that does not mean it is real. It means you are being prepared for a larger transfer. The system is designed to let you win first — so you lose more later. **5. Pressure is the final stage before you lose money.** "Only today", "don't tell anyone", "this is exclusive", "I'm investing with you" — these are not opportunities. These are pressure mechanisms. Real financial decisions do not require urgency. If someone pushes you to act fast — stop immediately. **6. Video calls do not guarantee reality.** Modern tools allow faces to be altered or generated in real time. Even if you see a person on camera — it does not confirm who they are. What matters is not what you see — but what you are being asked to do next. **7. The simplest protection still works.** Before sending money: show the conversation to someone you trust, wait 24–48 hours, question why a stranger is offering you profit. Scammers rely on isolation and speed. Remove those — and the system breaks. --- ## Tools Used in This Investigation | Tool | Role in the investigation | |---|---| | **Telegram Username Lookup Bot** | Initial pivot — reverse lookup of the Telegram username to linked phone number | | **FunStat Telegram Bot** | Behavioural profiling — group memberships, subscription patterns, account age | | **Telegram Leak Bots** | Cross-referenced phone number against breach datasets — negative signal as evidence | | **Manuel Travezaño's Bot** | Primary enrichment — full name, additional phones, linked services from phone number | | **Reverse Face Search (Telegram Bot)** | Applied after controlled exposure — ~78% match linked to a social profile | | **OSINT Industries** | Email-based pivot — linked platforms, behavioural signals, indirect geolocation | | **Screen Recording** | Critical evidence acquisition — captured the real face during pre-shift exposure | All tools are legally accessible OSINT resources, but their effectiveness depends on sequence, timing, and correct pivoting. --- ## Final Thoughts When you look at cases like this, it is easy to call it "just another scam". That would be wrong. What we are dealing with is not individuals, but a **system** — structured, trained, and constantly evolving. These operations invest in psychology, technology, and process. They train operators, test scripts, refine approaches. This is not improvisation anymore. It is infrastructure. People do not lose money because they are careless. They lose because they are facing something **designed to work**. In this case, everything changed because of one moment — one mistake. A call accepted without verification. A fraction of a second where routine overrode control. That was enough. Everything that followed — face, identity, data — was not luck. It was the result of acting immediately when that moment appeared. That is the core of this work. OSINT is not about "finding people". It is about recognising when a system fails — even briefly — and knowing how to move faster than it recovers. We identified one operator — the lowest level in the structure. But every investigation starts the same way: one entry point, one identity, one connection. Follow it far enough, and the structure begins to unfold. I cannot say how this case progressed further or how it ultimately concluded. But I know this: **one person did not lose $30,000, one family did not lose stability, and someone who believed they were invisible is now part of a real investigation.** That is enough. Stay aware. Share this with someone who might need it — because while you are reading this, someone else is already inside that conversation, believing it is real.

The investigative methodology, tools, and operational approach described remain accurate and reflect real-world practice.

body_uk:
> Кейс з реальної практики скринінгу кандидата на чутливу позицію

### Про що цей кейс

У корпоративному скринінгу ми звикли до бездоганних резюме та чистих LinkedIn-профілів. Але реальність часто ховається за приватними акаунтами та **«другим життям»** у соціальних мережах.

Цей кейс показав, наскільки ефективним є підхід *family chain*: кандидат ретельно приховав власні профілі — але його рідні не приховали нічого. Це не удача. Це системна методологія.

---

### 🎯 Кандидат

| Атрибут | Що видно на поверхні |
|---|---|
| **Стать / вік** | Чоловік, 36 років |
| **Резюме** | Бездоганне, без пробілів |
| **Instagram** | Приватний. Сімейні фото, без геотегів, без облич дітей |
| **LinkedIn** | Виключно професійні дописи |
| **Гугл** | Нічого підозрілого |

**На поверхні** — ідеальний кандидат.
**У реальності** — навіть близько не так.

---

### 🔍 Крок 1 — Початковий збір: чому не просто Google

Я одразу почав з **OSINT Industries** + **спеціалізовані OSINT-агрегатори**.

**Чому саме ці інструменти:**

- **OSINT Industries** — 1000+ платформ, включно з регіональними. Один запит повертає 20–40 потенційних ідентифікаторів. У масових скринінгах це економить години.
- **Профільний OSINT-toolkit** — автоматизовані трансформи, перевірка старих і покинутих акаунтів. Знаходить ідентифікатори, які OSINT Industries пропускає.

> ⚠️ **Глухий кут №1:** основні профілі кандидата приватні або порожні.

**💡 Рішення:** Google Dorks — `повне_ім'я + "дружина / сім'я" site:facebook.com`. Знайшов старий Facebook дружини — вона залишила посилання на свій Instagram. Її профіль відкритий і привів до тегів та згадок її сестри.

---

### 🔓 Крок 2 — Витоки даних: чому BreachDirectory + HIBP разом

Старий email кандидата пішов на перевірку витоків.

- **Have I Been Pwned** — швидка перевірка у відомих великих витоках.
- **BreachDirectory** — індексує свіжі stealer-логи та комбо-списки. Email + Telegram-активність, яких немає у HIBP, з'являються тут.

> ⚠️ **Глухий кут №2:** прямий Telegram-username не знайшовся одразу.

**💡 Рішення:** reverse-lookup Telegram-інструменти за номером телефону з витоку. Номер привів до старих оголошень на місцевій дошці. В одному з них:

> *«Якщо мене немає — телефонуйте сестрі дружини»* + її номер.

Класичний півот: коли прямий слід холоне — шукай непрямі згадки в оголошеннях та форумах.

---

### 👨‍👩‍👧 Крок 3 — Розблокування через родину

Профіль сестри дружини — повністю відкритий.

Фото сімейної подорожі 2023 року — з підписом, що тегує кандидата під **другим ніком**.

*(username змінено з міркувань етики та анонімізації)*

**Те саме обличчя. Інша сторона життя.**

В Highlights — скріншоти високоризикової фінансової активності, дописи про нерегульовані транзакції, обмінники без верифікації.

---

### 📱 Крок 4 — Telegram: точка неповернення

Через номер сестри дружини + додаткові Telegram-боти знайдено **другий акаунт кандидата**. Активний у каналах, де обговорюються P2P-операції та обхід комплаєнсу.

Старий коментар під тим ніком:

> *«На роботі все під контролем. Ніхто так глибоко не копатиме.»*

> ⚠️ **Глухий кут №3:** основний Telegram закритий і чистий.

**💡 Рішення:** крос-перевірка за номером телефону + старими нікнеймами з витоків. Тримай у наборі кілька Telegram OSINT-ботів. Ніколи не зупиняйся на першому профілі.

---

### ✅ Результат: 2 години 10 хвилин

| Пункт | Висновок |
|---|---|
| **Різниця** | Між заявленим та реальним профілем — колосальна |
| **Комплаєнс** | Insider threat, ризик обходу процедур |
| **Вердикт** | 🚩 **Red flag** — не рекомендовано |

---

### 💡 Головний висновок

**90 % людей** думають, що заховалися, закривши власний Instagram.

Але рідні — дружини, сестри, матері — майже ніколи не закривають свої профілі повністю. Вони **тегують усіх**. Публікують сімейні фото. Залишають старі номери телефонів у старих оголошеннях.

> Один відкритий сімейний пост — і весь ланцюжок розплітається.

---

### 📌 Що варто взяти собі HR та безпековим командам

- **Родинна перевірка** — завжди перевіряй цифровий слід близьких при скринінгу на чутливі посади.
- **Оголошення** — місцеві дошки містять старі телефони та контакти, про які люди забувають.
- **Бази витоків** — розкривають зв'язки між ідентичностями на різних платформах, а не тільки паролі.
- **«Чистий профіль»** — це не кінець розслідування. Це його початок.

---

*Усі дані анонімізовано. Методологія використовує виключно відкриті джерела публічної інформації. Кейси описано з фокусом на методологію, без розголошення конфіденційної інформації клієнта.*

> A detailed case study from real practice — candidate screening for a sensitive position

In corporate screening, we've grown used to flawless resumes and clean LinkedIn profiles. But reality often hides behind private accounts and a "second life" on social media.

This case showed how effective the family chain approach can be: the candidate carefully hid his profiles — but his relatives didn't. This isn't luck. It's a systematic methodology.

### 🎯 The Candidate

Male, 36. Flawless resume. Private Instagram — family photos, no geotags, no children's faces. LinkedIn — professional posts only.

On the surface: an ideal candidate. In reality: not even close.

### 🔍 Stage 1 — Initial Collection: Why Not Just Google

I started immediately with **OSINT Industries** + **спеціалізовані OSINT-агрегатори**.

- **OSINT Industries** — 1000+ platforms including regional ones. One query returns 20–40 potential identifiers. In bulk screenings this saves hours.
- **Профільний OSINT-toolkit** — Automated transforms, checks for old and abandoned accounts.

> ⚠️ **Dead end #1:** Candidate's main profiles were private or empty.

**💡 Solution:** Google Dorks — `full_name + "wife / family" site:facebook.com`. Found the wife's old Facebook — she had left a link to her Instagram. Her profile was open and led to tags and mentions of her sister.

### 🔓 Stage 2 — Breach Data: Why BreachDirectory + HIBP Together

- **Have I Been Pwned** — Fast check against major known breaches.
- **BreachDirectory** — Indexes fresh stealer logs and combo lists.

> ⚠️ **Dead end #2:** Direct Telegram username didn't appear immediately.

**💡 Solution:** reverse-lookup Telegram tools by phone number from the leak. The number led to old listings on a local classified ads platform. In one: *"if I'm not available — call my wife's sister"* + her number.

### 👨‍👩‍👧 Stage 3 — The Family Unlock

The wife's sister's profile was fully open. A 2023 family trip photo — with a caption tagging the candidate under a secondary nickname.

*(username changed for ethical and anonymisation purposes)*

Same face. Different life. Highlights contained screenshots of high-risk financial activity, posts about unregulated transactions, exchanges with no verification process.

### 📱 Stage 4 — Telegram: Point of No Return

Through the sister-in-law's number + additional Telegram bots — found the candidate's second account. Active in channels discussing P2P operations and compliance bypass.

In old comments under his alias:

> *"Everything is under control at work. No one will dig that deep."*

> ⚠️ **Dead end #3:** Main Telegram was closed and clean.

**💡 Solution:** Cross-check by phone number + old usernames from leaks. Always keep several Telegram OSINT bots in the toolkit. Never stop at the first profile.

### ✅ Result: 2 hours 10 minutes

- **Discrepancy** between stated and actual activity
- **Compliance** and insider threat risk
- **Verdict** — 🚩 **Red flag** recommendation

### 💡 The Main Lesson

90% of people think they've hidden themselves by closing their own Instagram. But relatives — wives, sisters, mothers — almost never close their profiles completely. They tag everyone. They post family photos. They leave old phone numbers in listings.

> One open family post. The entire chain unravels.

### 📌 Practical Takeaways for HR & Security Teams

- **Family check** — Always check the digital footprint of immediate family when screening for sensitive positions
- **Classified ads** — These platforms contain old phone numbers and contact details people forget about
- **Breach databases** — Reveal identity links across platforms — not just passwords
- **Clean profile** — A "clean" main profile is not the end of the investigation. It's the beginning.

*All data has been anonymised. The methodology uses exclusively open-source public information.*

body_uk:
> Case study · OSINT · SOCMINT · Attribution фейкового профілю · Тільки відкриті джерела До мене звернувся клієнт — батько чотирнадцятирічної доньки. Три тижні його дочка листується у Direct з акаунтом, який представився сімнадцятирічним хлопцем; треба встановити тип акаунта — реальна людина чи операція — і масштаб. На вході — один Instagram-username. Аватарка 320×320. Три слова у bio. Нічого більше.
⚠️ Усі персональні дані повністю анонімізовано: username, ім'я клієнта і доньки, географія, реальні скріншоти — не публікуються. Замість зачорнених реальних скрінів використовую **згенеровані ілюстрації-мокапи**, які точно відтворюють вигляд і поведінку інструментів, але не містять жодного реального елемента (ні дат, ні хешів, ні UI-версій, ні характерних маркерів акаунту). Причина проста: навіть добре зачорнений реальний скрін іноді лишає непрямі сліди — конкретну версію інтерфейсу, часову мітку у куті, рідкісний layout-баг. Мокап знімає це питання повністю. Методологія і послідовність кроків — 1-в-1 як у роботі. Всі інструменти публічні, працюють на відкритих даних, без обходу приватності. Для перегляду followers/following використовувався мій прогрітий (3+ місяців реалістичної активності) sockpuppet-акаунт; свіжий IG прикриває перегляд списків уже після 20-30 запитів.
--- ### 🎯 Мета Визначити чи це реальний одноліток, а якщо ні — з чим маємо справу (одинак чи структура) і як батьку діяти з дочкою, не штовхнувши її в оборону. --- ### 🖼️ Крок 1 — Аватарка Скачав аватарку в оригіналі. EXIF пусто — очікувано, IG re-encode'ить фото при завантаженні. Прогнав через п'ять реверсів різного призначення: - **TinEye** — літеральні копії файлу у веб-індексі. Мовчить: файл перезакодовано. - **Google Lens** — general-purpose reverse image, у 2026 де-факто стандарт для non-face контексту (фон, вивіски, вирізки). На чисто-портретній аватарці нічого корисного — очікувано. - **FaceCheck.ID** — face-engine по відкритому вебу. Знайшов те саме обличчя в архіві модельного агентства. Безкоштовний тир показує лише факт наявності matches; повні URL — за платні кредити. - **Yandex Images** — робочий безкоштовний backup для UA/RU-контексту. Дає збіг зі стоковим каталогом, дата завантаження у сток — 2019. - **Search4Faces** — VK/OK кеш; оновлення VK-індексу деградували з 2022 через блокування скрейпінгу, тому актуальні акаунти сервіс не бачить. Знайшов те саме обличчя як аватарку у 40+ VK-акаунтів, створених 2020–2023. ![Face-search стек — чотири вкладки з результатами по одній аватарці: FaceCheck.ID, Yandex Images (сток-каталог), Search4Faces (40+ VK), TinEye (порожньо)](/img/uploads/cases/fake-teen-ig-01-face-search.png) > **Що це показує:** одна аватарка — не власна. Обличчя роками ротується у десятках профілів. Reuse-pattern підтверджений. --- ### 👤 Крок 2 — Профіль Через sockpuppet — просто очима (IG у 2026 не віддає повний followers/following навіть warm-акаунту; видимі перші ~200 через пагінацію, цього тут вистачає): - Створений 23 дні тому. - Слідкує за 47 акаунтами: переважна більшість — дівчата приблизно 13-16 (за bio, шкільними маркерами, візуалом). Географія «дві області України» виведена не з нашого профілю (bio порожнє), а з геотегів у постах його follow-листа та згадок шкіл у їхніх bio. - Слідкують за ним — 12 акаунтів; 8 з них теж мають ознаки фейків. - Bio — три слова. Без емодзі, без міста, без школи. - 8 постів, всі «естетичні», обличчя не видно на 6 з них. ![Instagram-профіль через sockpuppet — bio з трьох слів, 8 «естетичних» постів, метрики followers/following, дата створення](/img/uploads/cases/fake-teen-ig-02-profile.jpg) > **Що це показує:** підліток за три тижні генерує 30 сторіс, підписується на клас. Тут — стерильна структура: точкова аудиторія, мінімум слідів, обличчя ховається у власних постах. Профіль оптимізовано під вузьку аудиторію, без побутових слідів. --- ### 🕵️ Крок 3 — Username по кросплатформі Стандартний sanity-check перед побудовою гіпотез: - **WhatsMyName** (~600 платформ) — нуль. - **Maigret** (3000+ платформ) — нуль. Ні TikTok, ні Threads, ні Bluesky, ні Discord, ні жодного форуму. Абсолютний нуль колізій. ![Maigret CLI output — сотні перевірених платформ, для кожної NOT FOUND, підсумок «0 accounts found»](/img/uploads/cases/fake-teen-ig-03-maigret.png) > **Що це показує:** реальний підліток за 17 років лишить username-сліди у 5-15 сервісах. Нуль колізій означає, що **саме цей username** створений разово під цю операцію; про історію самого оператора це не говорить (у нього могли бути десятки інших ніків). Це не доказ ферми, але прибирає «звичайного підлітка» з ймовірностей. --- ### 🔗 Крок 4 — Патерн і синхронність Не копаю глибше у один акаунт — дивлюся убік. Беру унікальні маркери (аватарку, точні три слова з bio, характерний фільтр постів) і шукаю повтори. Знайшов ще 6 акаунтів. Різні username, той самий портрет з того самого модельного архіву (з ротацією між кількома фото одного моделі). У кожного — те саме bio у 2-3 варіаціях. Кожен створений у межах останніх 4 тижнів. Аудиторія кожного — 40-60 дівчат 13-16 з тих самих двох областей. Стягую публічну хронологію постів, stories і коментарів по всіх сімох. Timestamp лайків для чужих акаунтів у 2026 непублічний, тому працюю з тим, що є. Малюнок: - Пости виходять двома вікнами — 09:00-11:00 і 17:00-19:00 за Києвом. Синхронно у всіх сімох. - Активність у сторіс і коментарях — переважно 02:00-04:00 за Києвом. ![Grid із 7 паралельних IG-профілів + heatmap активності по годинах Kyiv-time з нічним і денним піками](/img/uploads/cases/fake-teen-ig-04-pattern.png) > **Що це показує:** спільний контент-стек — доведено. Спільний оператор — робоча гіпотеза, найкраще пояснена жвавою активністю у поясі приблизно UTC+5-6 години від Києва. Альтернативи не виключені: VPN оператора, автоматизація через scheduler, розподілена команда. Щоб їх виключити, потрібні дані, яких у публічному доступі немає, тому пріоритезація «одна група у одному поясі» лишається робочою гіпотезою, а не встановленим фактом. --- ### 📱 Крок 5 — Донор фотографій На двох постах помітив ледь помітний watermark у кутку фонового зображення. Пошук по фрагменту watermark у Google (комбо точних слів + кроп) вивів на рекламне оголошення в іншому публічному Telegram-каналі, який просуває пакети «естетичних портретів для соцмереж». За посиланням — інвайт у закритий канал з ~4 000 підписників. У закритому каналі, у пінному пості — відкритий прайс. Пакет 30 фото + готове bio: $15-40 залежно від «легенди». First-hand: я особисто увійшов у канал і побачив прайс — це one-vendor sample для цього каналу, не ринкова медіана. ![Telegram-канал з пінним постом-прайсом на пакети з фото і bio-шаблонами, метрика ~4000 підписників](/img/uploads/cases/fake-teen-ig-05-telegram.png) > **Що це показує:** це не полювання на людину — це погляд у ринок. Той, хто ліпить профілі, купує пакет як маркетолог купує креативи. --- ### 📄 Крок 6 — Що це і що ми зробили Складаю: - Обличчя — з покупного пакета. - Аудиторія — підлітки з двох областей. - Патерн — 7 акаунтів за 4 тижні, синхронна активність. - Часовий пояс живої активності — робоча гіпотеза UTC+5-6. - Постачальник контенту — комерційний Telegram-канал з тарифами. - Мета за листуванням — швидке зближення → перехід у Telegram («тут незручно писати»). Це не «дорослий чоловік, який видає себе за підлітка». Це маленький бізнес-процес: 7 профілів × ~45 контактів = ~300 у списку. Навіть за консервативної оцінки конверсії ризик для списку такого розміру не нульовий у горизонті кількох тижнів. Термінологічна поправка: у контексті таргету підліткової дівчинки коректніше говорити не про «класичну» sextortion (яка у 2025 переважно цілиться в хлопців з фінансовою вимогою), а про **grooming + image-based coercion**. Що зробили: - Не забирати телефон, не влаштовувати сцен, не показувати доньці цей звіт напряму. - Показати їй що аватарка з стоку — це верифіковано, а не «я думаю». Не про безпеку. Про facts. - Сповістити класного керівника з патерном: паралельні класи можуть бути в тому ж списку. - Скринити переписку і зафіксувати за протоколом на випадок CyberPolice. - Meta-репорт на всі 7 акаунтів з формулюванням impersonation + coordinated inauthentic behavior і докладеною доказовою базою (side-by-side аватарок, синхронність timestamps). Meta реагує стохастично; якісна доказова база підвищує пріоритет review, але не гарантує результат — за тиждень з семи знято три. Дочка перечитала звіт і мовчки видалила листування. > **Що це показує:** цінність OSINT-роботи тут — не «зловити зловмисника», а «дати сім'ї підстави для розмови». Батьку без цих доказів довелось би нависати над донькою або мовчати. Ми дали факти, з якими дитина сама зробила висновок. --- ### 🏆 Фінальний зріз | Пункт | Висновок | |---|---| | «17-річний хлопець» на фото | Обличчя з модельного архіву, у сток-каталозі з 2019 | | Профіль | 23 дні, стерильна структура, слідкує за ~50 дівчатами підліткового віку у двох областях UA | | Nickname на інших платформах | Нуль колізій — username створений разово під операцію | | Патерн | 7 паралельних акаунтів, спільний контент-стек (доведено), синхронна активність (підтверджує спільного оператора як гіпотезу) | | Часовий пояс оператора | Робоча гіпотеза UTC+5-6, не факт | | Джерело контенту | Комерційний Telegram-канал, тарифи $15-40 (first-hand) | | Мета | Grooming + image-based coercion (інтерпретація) | | Загроза для доньки | Пряма, але не персональна — статистична (за галузевою аналогією) | **Ланцюг півотів:** аватарка → face-search + сток → username-nullifier → патерн 7 акаунтів → синхронний часовий патерн → Telegram-постачальник. --- ### 💡 Ключові висновки 1. **Одна аватарка — вже цифровий слід.** У професійних реверсах 2026 (FaceCheck.ID, Yandex, Search4Faces) 320×320 достатньо, щоб зчепитися з історією фото за 5-7 років назад. 2. **Патерн важливіший за окремий факт.** Один підозрілий акаунт — це людина. Сім однакових — процес. 3. **Розділяй «content-supplier» і «оператор».** Один пакет може крутити один менеджер із сімома вкладками або сім незалежних покупців. Це різні поради клієнту. 4. **Час активності — біометрія з обмеженнями.** Timestamp постів і сторіс — хороший сигнал для гіпотези про пояс. VPN, scheduler, розподілена команда — реальні альтернативи. 5. **Правильна назва об'єкта визначає відповідь.** «Педофіл-одинак» і «оператор ферми» вимагають різних стратегій. OSINT дає батькові правильну назву проблеми. --- ### 🎭 Про мотив Це не «злий чоловік у підвалі». Це низовий комерційний сегмент ринку — з тарифами, змінами оператора і кросплатформною логістикою. За скріншотом «17-річного хлопця» стоїть чат-канал з 4 000 підписників, ціна пакета $15-40, менеджер, оператор із сімома вкладками. Це не робить оператора менш небезпечним. Але це змінює розмову з донькою: не «мене вибрали, бо я особлива», а «нас 300 у списку». Це відпускає провину — і дає простір для дорослої розмови без страху й істерики. ---
⚠️ Усі техніки — з арсеналу публічних, відкритих OSINT-інструментів. Жоден акаунт не був зламаний, жоден пароль не був отриманий, жодні приватні повідомлення не читалися без згоди учасника. Sockpuppet-акаунт використовувався виключно для перегляду публічних елементів (followers, following, пости, stories) без взаємодії з ким-небудь.

> Case study · OSINT · SOCMINT · Fake profile attribution · Open sources only A client came to me — the father of a fourteen-year-old girl. For three weeks his daughter has been messaging in Direct with an account that presented itself as a seventeen-year-old boy; I need to establish the type of account — a real person or an operation — and its scale. Inputs: one Instagram username. Avatar 320×320. Three words in the bio. Nothing else.
⚠️ All personal data fully anonymised: the username, the client's and daughter's names, the geography, and real screenshots are not published. Instead of blurred-out real screenshots I use **generated mockup illustrations** that faithfully reproduce the look and behaviour of the tools without containing any real element (no dates, no hashes, no UI versions, no distinctive account markers). The reason is simple: even a well-redacted real screenshot occasionally leaves indirect traces — a specific interface version, a timestamp in a corner, a rare layout bug. Mockups remove this concern completely. The methodology and step sequence are 1-for-1 as in the actual work. All tools are public and operate on open data, without bypassing privacy. Follower/following lists were viewed through a warmed sockpuppet account (3+ months of realistic activity); a fresh IG account gets its list-viewing clamped after 20-30 requests.
--- ### 🎯 Goal Three things, in this order: 1. Determine whether this is a real peer of the daughter — or someone else. 2. If not a peer — assess the level of threat (a lone individual lying about age, or a structured operation). 3. Give the father a strategy for talking with his daughter without pushing her into a defensive stance. Simple to state. Turned out — not so simple to execute. --- ### 🖼️ Step 1 — The avatar Downloaded the avatar at native resolution. EXIF empty — expected, Instagram re-encodes photos on upload. Ran it through five reverses, each with a different job: - **TinEye** — literal file/crop copies in the web index since 2008. Silent: file was re-encoded. - **Google Lens** — general-purpose reverse image, by 2026 the de-facto standard for non-face context (background, signage, cutouts). Nothing useful on a pure portrait avatar — as expected. - **FaceCheck.ID** — face engine over the open web. Found the same face in a modelling-agency archive. Free tier shows only that matches exist; full URLs live behind a paid tier. - **Yandex Images** — a working free backup for the UA/RU context. Returned a match against a stock catalogue with an upload date of 2019. - **Search4Faces** — VK/OK cache; VK index updates degraded from 2022 due to scraping blocks, so the service does not see current accounts. Found the same face used as avatar in 40+ VK accounts created between 2020 and 2023. ![Face-search stack — four tabs of results on one avatar: FaceCheck.ID, Yandex Images (stock catalogue), Search4Faces (40+ VK), TinEye (empty)](/img/uploads/cases/fake-teen-ig-01-face-search.png) > **What this shows:** the avatar isn't his own. The face has been rotating for years across dozens of profiles. The reuse pattern is confirmed. --- ### 👤 Step 2 — The profile Through the sockpuppet — plain eyes (Instagram in 2026 does not return the full followers/following list even to a warm account; the first ~200 are visible via pagination, which is enough here): - Created 23 days ago. - Following 47 accounts: the majority — by bio, school markers, and visual cues — appear to be girls roughly 13-16. The "two regions of Ukraine" geography is not inferred from this profile (its bio is empty) but from geotags in the follow-list's posts and from school names in those followers' bios. - Followed by 12 accounts; 8 of them also show fake markers. - Bio — three words. No emoji, no city, no school. - 8 posts, all "aesthetic", face not visible on 6 of them. ![Instagram profile via sockpuppet — three-word bio, 8 "aesthetic" posts, followers/following stats, creation date](/img/uploads/cases/fake-teen-ig-02-profile.jpg) > **What this shows:** a teenager generates 30 stories in three weeks, follows their class, sprays likes without thinking. Here — a sterile structure: narrow target audience, minimal traces, face hidden even in own posts. This profile is optimised for a narrow audience, without any everyday traces. --- ### 🕵️ Step 3 — Username across platforms The standard sanity-check before building hypotheses: - **WhatsMyName** (about 600 platforms) — zero. - **Maigret** (3000+ platforms) — zero. Not on TikTok, not on Threads, not on Bluesky, not on Discord, not on any forum. Absolute zero collisions. ![Maigret CLI output — hundreds of platforms checked, each NOT FOUND, summary "0 accounts found"](/img/uploads/cases/fake-teen-ig-03-maigret.png) > **What this shows:** an OSINT reader recognises this signal at once. A real seventeen-year-old will leave username traces in 5-15 services over their life — Steam, Discord, TikTok, an old Roblox account, a Reddit repost, anything. **Absolute zero collisions means that this specific username was created one-off for this operation and has no history of its own — this says nothing about the operator's own history; they could easily have dozens of other handles.** It is still not proof of a farm (a paranoid-OPSEC lone individual could do the same), but it removes "an ordinary teenager" from the probability space. --- ### 🔗 Step 4 — Pattern and synchronicity Rather than digging deeper into a single account, I look sideways. Take the unique markers — the exact avatar, the exact three words in the bio, the characteristic post filter — and search for repeats. Found another 6 accounts. Different usernames, different display names, the same portrait from the same modelling archive (with rotation across a few photos of the same young model). Every one has the same bio in 2-3 variations. Every one was created within the last 4 weeks. The audience of each — 40-60 girls aged 13-16 in the same two regions. At this point it matters to stop and not to jump to a conclusion. Seven accounts sharing content admit two equally-valid explanations: - **Shared operator** — a single farm produces seven profiles in parallel. - **Shared supplier** — seven independent buyers purchased the same content pack. **Shared content-supplier is proven.** Shared operator is a working hypothesis that needs a separate test (see Step 5, activity synchronicity). Pull the public timeline of posts, stories, and comments across all seven. Like timestamps for third-party accounts are non-public in 2026, so I work with what is available. The pattern: - Posts drop in two windows — 09:00-11:00 and 17:00-19:00 Kyiv time. Synchronous across all seven. - Story and comment activity is concentrated overnight in Kyiv time, 02:00-04:00. ![Grid of 7 parallel IG profiles + activity heatmap by hours (Kyiv time) with night and day peaks](/img/uploads/cases/fake-teen-ig-04-pattern.png) > **What this shows:** shared content stack — proven. Shared operator — a working hypothesis best explained by live activity in a time zone approximately UTC+5-6 from Kyiv. Alternatives are not excluded: operator VPN, automation via scheduler, distributed team. To rule those out one needs data that isn't publicly available, so prioritising "one team in one time zone" stays a working hypothesis, not an established fact. --- ### 📱 Step 5 — The content donor Back to the avatar and the rest of the posts. Reverse-image and face-search already pointed to a stock catalogue and a modelling archive; what was left was where exactly this content gets bulk-sourced for this specific farm. On two posts I noticed a faint watermark — not on the avatar, but in the corner of a background image. Searching that watermark via Google (a combo of exact-word phrases and image crop) led to a promotional post in another public Telegram channel selling packs of "aesthetic portraits for social media". The link — an invite into a closed channel of about 4,000 subscribers. Inside the closed channel, the pinned message is an open price list. A pack of 30 photos plus a ready-made bio: $15-40 depending on the "legend". First-hand: I joined the channel personally and read the pricing — this is a one-vendor sample for that channel, not a market median. ![Telegram channel with a pinned pricing post for photo + bio packs, subscribers count ~4000](/img/uploads/cases/fake-teen-ig-05-telegram.png) > **What this shows:** you are not hunting a person. You are looking at a market. Whoever assembles these profiles buys the pack the way a marketer buys creatives. --- ### 📄 Step 6 — What this is, and what we did Putting it together: - Face — from a purchased pack. - Audience — teenagers in two regions. - Pattern — 7 accounts in 4 weeks, synchronous activity. - Live-activity time zone — working hypothesis UTC+5-6. - Content supplier — a commercial Telegram channel with a tariff sheet. - Goal per the chat — quick rapport, transition to Telegram ("it's uncomfortable here to text"). This is not "an adult man pretending to be a teenager". This is a small business process: 7 profiles × ~45 contacts = ~300 people on the list. Even under a conservative conversion estimate, the risk for a list of that size is non-zero over a horizon of a few weeks. A terminological correction: for a teenage female target it is more accurate to speak not of "classic" sextortion (which in 2025 primarily targets boys with financial demands) but of **grooming + image-based coercion**. What we did: - Do not take the phone away. Do not stage a scene. Do not show the daughter this report directly. - Show her that the avatar was assembled from stock imagery — it is verified, not a guess. Not about safety. About facts. - Alert the class supervisor with the pattern: parallel classes may be on the same list. - Screenshot the whole chat and log it to a protocol (metadata, dates, timestamps) in case CyberPolice needs it. - Meta reports on all 7 accounts framed as impersonation + coordinated inauthentic behaviour with a full evidence package (side-by-side avatars, timestamp synchronicity). Meta reacts stochastically; a well-structured evidence package raises review priority but does not guarantee an outcome — three of seven were taken down within a week. The daughter re-read the report and quietly deleted the chat. > **What this shows:** the value of the OSINT work here isn't "catching the perpetrator" — it is "giving the family a basis for a conversation". Without those facts the father would have had to hover over the daughter or stay silent and watch. We gave a third option: facts the child herself used to reach a conclusion. --- ### 🏆 Final summary | Item | Finding | |---|---| | "17-year-old boy" in the photo | Face from a modelling archive, in a stock catalogue since 2019 | | Profile | 23 days old, sterile structure, follows ~50 teenage-age girls in two regions of Ukraine | | Username on other platforms | Zero collisions — created one-off for the operation | | Pattern | 7 parallel accounts, shared content stack (proven), synchronous activity (supports shared operator as a hypothesis) | | Operator time zone | Working hypothesis UTC+5-6, not a fact | | Content source | Commercial Telegram channel, tariffs $15-40 (first-hand) | | Goal | Grooming + image-based coercion (interpretation) | | Threat to the daughter | Direct, but not personal — statistical (by industry analogy) | **Pivot chain:** avatar → face-search + stock → username-nullifier → pattern of 7 accounts → synchronous time pattern → Telegram supplier. --- ### 💡 Key takeaways 1. **A single avatar is already a full digital trace.** In professional 2026 reverses (FaceCheck.ID, Yandex, Search4Faces) 320×320 is enough to hook into 5-7 years of photo history. The "there's nothing visible on my avatar" argument holds up worse every year. 2. **Pattern beats a single fact.** One suspicious account is a person. Seven identical accounts are a process. 3. **Separate "content supplier" from "operator".** The same content pack can be run by a single manager with seven tabs, or by seven independent buyers. These are different advisories to the client. 4. **Activity time is biometrics — with caveats.** Post and story timestamps are a strong signal for time-zone hypotheses. VPN, scheduler, and distributed teams are real alternatives that cannot be ignored. 5. **The right name for the object determines the answer.** "Lone paedophile" and "farm operator" require different defensive strategies. OSINT gives the father the correct name of the problem. --- ### 🎭 On motive This is not "an evil man in a basement". It is a low-tier commercial market segment — with tariffs, operator shifts, and cross-platform logistics. Behind the screenshot of a "17-year-old boy" stands a channel with 4,000 subscribers, a pack priced at $15-40, a manager, an operator with seven tabs. That does not make the operator less dangerous. But it changes the conversation with the daughter: not "I was picked because I'm special", but "we are 300 on a list". That releases the guilt — and gives space for an adult conversation without fear and without hysteria. ---
⚠️ All techniques are drawn from the public, open OSINT toolkit. No account was hacked, no password was obtained, no private messages were read without the participant's consent. The sockpuppet account was used only to view public elements (followers, following, posts, stories) without interacting with anyone.

title_uk: Кейс: атрибуція особи з одного цифрового ідентифікатора
title_en: Case Study: Identity Correlation from a Single Numeric Identifier
summary_uk: Одне число — Telegram ID. Через історію username, крос-платформну кореляцію, витік контактних даних, старе CV, аналіз email і активність у Google Maps — реконструкція реальної особи та спростування заявленої країни проживання. Менше ніж за 3 години.
summary_en: A single number — Telegram ID. Through username history, cross-platform correlation, contact leakage, an old CV, email analysis, and Google Maps activity — reconstruction of the real identity and disproving the stated country of residence. Under 3 hours.
body_uk:
> Методологія · Тільки відкриті джерела · Менше ніж за 3 години Відштовхуючись від єдиного Telegram ID, кейс показує, як фрагментовані відкриті дані можна системно поєднати, щоб реконструювати ідентичність і перевірити задекларовану інформацію.
⚠️ Усі дані у статті анонімізовано. Telegram ID 483920174651 вигаданий. Скріншоти підготовано відповідно до етичних принципів OSINT.
--- ### 📜 Крок 1 — Telegram ID → історія username Перший крок — витягнути історичні ідентифікатори акаунту, прив'язані до числового Telegram ID. Це розкриває **хронологію попередніх нікнеймів і патерни активності**, які часто зберігаються навіть після зміни акаунту. - Повна історія всіх коли-небудь використаних username — з датами змін - Статистика активності — у публічних групах та каналах - Патерни повідомлень Це стало відправною точкою для подальшого крос-платформного дослідження. Історія username у Telegram часто залишається доступною навіть після видалення або зміни handle. ![Telegram-аналітичний бот — історія username та статистика акаунту](/img/uploads/cases/numeric-id-step1.png) --- ### 🔗 Крок 2 — крос-платформна кореляція username Виявлені алиаси було співставлено на кількох платформах для виявлення патернів повторного використання та зв'язків між акаунтами. Цей крок дозволив побудувати **крос-платформний граф ідентичності** на основі послідовного повторного використання username. Один зі співставлених профілів містив публічно розкриту контактну інформацію, що стало ключовою точкою розвороту для подальшого аналізу. ![Крос-платформний OSINT-агрегатор — огляд платформ](/img/uploads/cases/numeric-id-step2.png) ![OSINT Industries — граф зв'язків між платформами](/img/uploads/cases/numeric-id-step3.png) --- ### 📱 Крок 3 — збагачення контактних даних Публічно розкрита контактна інформація була використана для подальшого збагачення та атрибуції. Процес збагачення виявив послідовні ідентифікаційні маркери, включно з іменами та можливими географічними індикаторами. Один зі знайдених ідентифікаторів співпав з активним акаунтом у соцмережі, що посилило атрибуцію. ![GetContact — результат по номеру телефону](/img/uploads/cases/numeric-id-step4.png) --- ### 📄 Крок 4 — пошук за реальним ім'ям → CV та університетські записи Маючи ідентифіковане повне ім'я, точковий пошук по точному збігу дозволив виявити публічно доступні академічні та професійні записи. Пошук швидко повернув: - Профіль студента університету - Публічно доступне резюме (PDF) У резюме в розділі контактів був вказаний персональний email. Показово, що це вимагало лише базових пошукових технік — це підкреслює вразливість відкрито проіндексованих даних. --- ### ✉️ Крок 5 — email → аналіз прив'язки акаунтів Ідентифікований email проаналізовано для визначення пов'язаних сервісів та прив'язки акаунтів. Аналіз показав прив'язку до активної екосистеми сервісів, включаючи платформи з геолокацією. ![Epieos — результат Google Account Finder (всі персональні дані приховані)](/img/uploads/cases/numeric-id-step5.png) --- ### 🗺️ Крок 6 — верифікація заявленої резиденції через геосигнали Аналіз метаданих локації, прив'язаних до акаунту, показав нещодавні патерни активності (в межах кількох днів), що вказувало на присутність у різних публічних місцях. Спостережена активність **географічно не збігалася** з публічно заявленою країною проживання суб'єкта. Ця розбіжність стала валідаційним сигналом — індикатором розбіжності між задекларованою інформацією і спостережуваними цифровими слідами. ![Google Maps — активність (анонімізовано)](/img/uploads/cases/numeric-id-step6.png) --- ### ⏱️ Загальний час Виконано в обмежений час — демонстрація ефективності структурованих OSINT-процесів під тиском таймінгу. --- ### 🔍 Професійні спостереження - **Числові платформні ідентифікатори** часто зберігають більш стійкий історичний зв'язок ніж user-facing handles, роблячи їх цінними точками пивоту на ранньому етапі - **User-generated marketplace content** — постійне джерело ненавмисно розкритих контактних даних - **Збагачення контактів** часто виявляє легасі-ідентифікатори (нікнейми, алиаси), що дозволяють крос-платформну кореляцію - **Навіть базові exact-match запити** можуть виявити високочутливі відкрито проіндексовані персональні записи — це підкреслює ризики надмірної експозиції академічних і професійних даних - **Метадані сервісів локації** можуть надавати непрямі валідаційні сигнали при оцінці узгодженості декларованої інформації - **Історичні ідентифікатори** часто переживають наміри користувача і стають ключовими анкорами для реконструкції цифрового сліду - **Експозиція контактних даних** — один з найслабших і найчастіше ігнорованих OPSEC-елементів - **Ефективна крос-платформна атрибуція** рідко базується на одному сильному сигналі — а на накопиченні та валідації множинних слабких індикаторів - **Кореляція ідентичностей в OSINT** — фундаментально процес імовірнісної валідації, а не детерміністичної ідентифікації - Маленькі, індивідуально незначущі точки даних колективно створюють високоімовірну атрибуцію, коли правильно скорельовані Цей воркфлоу демонструє, як фрагментовані, малочутливі точки даних можна системно поєднати у цілісний профіль ідентичності через структуровану OSINT-методологію. ---
⚠️ Етична нотатка: усі дані анонімізовані та частково вигадані для демонстраційних цілей. Використано виключно публічно доступні джерела. Жодних приватних баз, витоків чи платних розвід-сервісів. Повна відповідність OSINT-етиці.

> Methodology · Open-Source Only · Under 3 Hours Starting from a single Telegram ID, this case shows how fragmented open-source data can be systematically correlated to reconstruct an identity and assess declared information.
⚠️ All data in this article has been anonymized. The Telegram ID 483920174651 is fictional.
### 📜 Step 1 — Telegram ID → Username History The initial step focused on extracting historical account identifiers associated with the numeric Telegram ID. This revealed a timeline of previously used aliases and activity patterns, which are often preserved even after account changes. ![Telegram analytics bot — username history and account statistics](/img/uploads/cases/numeric-id-step1.png) ### 🔗 Step 2 — Cross-Platform Username Correlation The identified aliases were then correlated across multiple platforms to detect reuse patterns and account linkages. This step enabled building a cross-platform identity graph based on consistent username reuse. ![Cross-platform OSINT aggregator — platform overview](/img/uploads/cases/numeric-id-step2.png) ![OSINT Industries platform](/img/uploads/cases/numeric-id-step3.png) ### 📱 Step 3 — Contact Data Enrichment Publicly exposed contact information was used for further enrichment and attribution. The enrichment process revealed consistent identity markers, including naming patterns and possible geographic indicators. ![GetContact — result for the phone number](/img/uploads/cases/numeric-id-step4.png) ### 📄 Step 4 — Real-Name Search → CV and University Records Using the identified full name, a targeted exact-match search allowed identification of publicly available academic and professional records. The search quickly returned a university student profile page and a publicly available CV (PDF). ### ✉️ Step 5 — Email → Account Linkage Analysis The identified email address was analyzed to determine associated services and account linkages. The analysis indicated linkage to an active ecosystem of services, including location-enabled platforms. ![Epieos — Google account finder result](/img/uploads/cases/numeric-id-step5.png) ### 🗺️ Step 6 — Verification of Stated Residence via Location Signals Analysis of location-related metadata associated with the account revealed recent activity patterns, indicating presence in various public venues. The observed activity was geographically inconsistent with the subject's publicly stated country of residence. ![Google Maps activity — anonymized](/img/uploads/cases/numeric-id-step6.png) ### 🔍 Professional Observations - Numeric platform identifiers often retain more persistent historical linkage than user-facing handles - User-generated marketplace content remains a consistent source of unintentionally exposed contact data - Historical identifiers often outlive user intent and become key anchors for reconstructing digital footprints - Identity correlation in OSINT is fundamentally a process of probabilistic validation, not deterministic identification
